source.snippet: We are using PowerMTA and have recently warmed up new IPs. During the last 2 days, Yahoo/AOL has been returning TSS04 and TSS05 temporary deferrals even on the first emails sent from these IPs. Environment: PowerMTA Port 25 delivery, Proper SPF, DKIM, and rDNS configured, Low sending volume during warm-up, No known complaint history on the new IPs.

problem_statement: Email infrastructure operators using PowerMTA face opaque and inconsistent temporary deferrals (TSS04/TSS05) from Yahoo/AOL on freshly warmed IPs, with no clear diagnostic tooling to identify root cause or predict when deliverability will recover.
target_segment: Email deliverability engineers and marketing operations teams at mid-to-large companies running dedicated email infrastructure (PowerMTA, Postfix) with high-volume sending requirements
notes: Business context is strong — PowerMTA is an enterprise-grade paid product; users are professionals managing high-volume sending infrastructure. TSS04/TSS05 errors are a recurring complaint in email ops communities. Opportunity: a deliverability monitoring + diagnostics SaaS that tracks deferral codes, benchmarks recovery timelines, and surfaces actionable remediation steps. Existing tools (MXToolbox, GlockApps, Postmaster Tools) don't cover PowerMTA-specific deferral pattern analysis. Clear willingness-to-pay given existing spend on PowerMTA licenses.
